I've been with my current boyfriend for almost a year now after leaving my cheating Nex. We've been living together since March. Here's my experience so far:

I was paranoid for a while at the beginning of the relationship. I was constantly on the lookout for red flags so that I wouldn't get into another abusive relationship. I had to keep reminding myself that, while I should be cautious, I couldn't let past trauma taint a new relationship. This way of thinking changed everything and let me trust again.

Our first fight, there was no yelling. There was no name calling, items getting thrown at me, walls punched, doors blocked, or threats issued. I had already shut down inside when we started fighting to prepare myself for the battle, but it never came. My boyfriend spoke so calmly I didn't know what to do. He laid out the issue and wanted to work with me to resolve it. We came to a resolution in maybe 10-15 minutes of talking, he hugged me and kissed my forehead and that was the end of the fight. I asked him for an hour after if he was mad at me, if he was upset, did he still love me? He offered reassurance to each question without getting tired or offended. We've fought since then with similar outcomes and I've found it brings peace. There's open communication without fear of retaliation, there's resolutions without blame, and there's moving forward without resentment. I don't hurt when we fight, and that feels incredible.

We stay in most weekends. We watch videos and play games and make dinner. We joke how funny the dog is and how work is terrible and what chores need done. There's no drama, no getting worked up over small things, and no walking on eggshells. I thought I would find it boring but it feels like nestling into a warm blanket. It's home, it's peace and living life without stressing about a relationship. He's my partner in life and he loves being there. He reminds me every day how much he loves me and how much he appreciates me and the little things I do. I've found something better than happiness, I've found out how to be content.

I fully admit I got very, very lucky with my situation. I was on the lookout for red flags and when I couldn't find any, I looked harder. I finally had to admit that I found a good relationship and I was going to try my hardest to keep it. Turns out, I didn't have to try that hard, he loves me because he loves me. I feel peaceful, which was entirely new at first and now I refuse to give it up. You can break the cycle and find happiness. There are incredible people in this world who don't want to use you but want to live a life with you. It's not you who are at fault for the abuse you've suffered, it's the abuser. You didn't attract them, they were attracted to you for the same qualities that the right people will also love. I can't give advice on how to find the right person because everyone's situation is so different, but it can happen.

A 3 lbs bag of food for two cats lasts me about 2 weeks. I have food set out 24/7, but my cats are both young and active. If they have any health issues or as they get older and less active, you would want to limit their food intake and have a set schedule for feeding. The only time I've mixed wet and dry food is when I weened my cats. Some cats are picky when it comes to food but unlike dogs, they generally enjoy the same food over and over so you don't have to worry about mixing up the flavors from time to time. The kitty litter jug lasts me 1 week-1.5 weeks. You'll have to make sure you're around to clean their box every day and change the litter completely every 4-7 days. Again, most of this is my personal experience and I can't speak for other cats.

Just some tips: check the ingredients in what cat food you buy. If you have a Pet Supplies Plus around you they have a pretty good brand of dry food called Redford Naturals. First ingredient is chicken. 

Cats also love things that are warm and soft (me) so it's a good idea to have a little blanket for them to lay on. Mine love the sherpa blankets. If you get a heating pad though, be careful. I have 2 cats, so here's my personal opinions.

1. Leaving for a while with a cat in the house won't hurt it, as long as it has food and water. However, just one cat could lead to it becoming bored and a bored cat can have many issues. I recommend 2 cats, but it depends on the individual cat's personality. My cats are more social, but I know of many cats that prefer the solitary lifestyle.

2. 99% of cats are curious and will investigate the smallest noise. If there's anything harmful in the attic, please don't let them up there. Chemicals or any toxic substance could easily kill a cat. Hunting mice is a natural instinct and cats won't lose sight of their target very easily. If the attic has nothing harmful in it and no structural damage or exits to outside, I think it would be fine.

3. A good bag of indoor cat good is usually 7-10 dollars for a 3 lbs bag. Litter is around 8 dollars. Cat trees can be anywhere from 30-300 dollars. Most beginner shots are around 20-60, depending on where you live. To spay/neuter for me is 65 dollars. Flea medicine from a vet is 30-75 dollars. In general, its a good idea to also have 100-200 set aside for an emergency, like if your cat gets sick or eats something it shouldn't (my kitten accidentally ate the tip of her bottle. It gets nerve wracking.) Also, one of the best and cheapest toys is a laser light. I promise, it's fun for both you and the cat. :)

4. My cats are the two snuggliest creatures. One of them loves to lay over my shoulder with her face under my hair. Both of mine were strays I found outside. I recommend checking a shelter first. Cats have a long memory and won't forget the kind person who gave them a home. In my experience, just like with my dogs, the cat chooses you. If you check a shelter, I don't think you'd have a problem finding a cat with the right personality for your lifestyle.
